title: Customer OPS: Replay consent lab notes and rollback paths
body:
Purpose and audience:

This is a compact customer-facing draft intended for two audiences: (1) customer success leads owning tenant outreach, and (2) engineering incident responders preparing a coordinated replay + rollback offer. The doc combines a status-page style summary with an opt-in replay consent flow and operator lab notes for validating evidence before executing rollbacks or replay runs.

Executive TL;DR (to appear on status page):
- Incident window: 2026-05-24 03:12–03:54 UTC.
- Impact: elevated token latency and occasional misordered streaming chunks for 3% of requests in eu-west-1. No data loss.
- Immediate mitigation: routing fallback and short-term cache flush rolled at 03:58 UTC; normal service restored by 04:20 UTC.
- Customer action choices: 1) no action, 2) opt into replay (evidence + sanitized replay), 3) request targeted rollback to prior model snapshot (enterprise only).

Scope & observed symptoms (lab notes):
- Root symptom: under high small-batch concurrency the runtime KV-merge path produced stale cache references leading to minor misorder in streaming frames.
- Affected tenants: 3% of tenants with heavy short inference patterns (<40 tokens). Identified tenant IDs attached in evidence bundle.
- Error surface: increased client-observed delta in response token ordering; in some long-living chat sessions, final assistant turn missed 1–2 prefix tokens.
- No authorization or user-data leakage detected. All telemetry and traces preserved.

What we did (chronology, condensed):
- 03:15 UTC: alerts (metric spike on streaming frame reorder).
- 03:22 UTC: SRE mitigations (temporarily widened batching window for hot-shard pools).
- 03:34 UTC: engineering reproduced locally in isolated lab using a replay harness (see evidence run IDs).
- 03:42 UTC: hotfix staged that gated KV-merge for short sequences.
- 03:58 UTC: routing fallback to unaffected model variants for high-risk tenants deployed.
- 04:20 UTC: metrics returned to baseline; monitoring watch initiated for 72h.

Customer choices and implications (decision ladder):
- Choice A — No action (default): No change to customer data. Most customers see no user-visible impact after 04:20 UTC. SRE will continue monitoring; SLA credits can be discussed if you experienced meaningful degradation.
- Choice B — Opt-in replay (recommended for customers who observed misordered/omitted tokens and want proof): We will run a scoped replay of affected requests using preserved request traces in a sanitized environment. Replay outputs will be packaged with diffs and a short annotation explaining fixes applied. Replay is opt-in and requires explicit consent via the consent form link below. Expect ~48–72hr turnaround.
- Choice C — Targeted rollback (enterprise only): For customers with regulatory needs or who prefer prior-model behavior, we can roll selected routes/tenants back to model snapshot v2026-05-20. Rollback requires scheduled maintenance window and a signed rollback request; performance tradeoffs may apply (slightly higher latency for some shapes).

Replay consent process (customer-facing):
- Step 1: Customer reviews the short consent form (link). The form explains sanitized data handling, minimal logs that will be accessed, and the exact tenant scope.
- Step 2: Customer selects replay lanes (time ranges or tenant IDs).
- Step 3: CS and Engineering confirm replay window and expected deliverables (diff package + summary).
- Step 4: Replay run in isolated lab; artifacts produced and delivered to customer via secure link.

Evidence & deliverables when opting in:
- A compact evidence bundle: request IDs, anonymized request/response pairs, reproduction scripts used in lab, and a short technical annotation.
- A human-readable summary: what changed, how the output differed, and recommended customer actions (if any).
- Optional: a short remediation walk-through call with eng + CS.

Risk notes and safeguards: (operator lab checklist)
- Ensure replay harness uses sanitized/obfuscated user content.
- Sanity-check diffs: Validate that any differences are limited to token ordering or truncation, not content hallucination.
- Rate-limit replay runs to preserve cluster capacity.
- Escalate to security if any PII patterns are detected during pre-replay scan.

Rollback path (if requested):
- Pre-reqs: signed rollback request, chosen maintenance window, expectation doc signed by customer.
- Steps: prepare snapshot, schedule canary for 10% of tenant traffic, monitor for 2h, then full roll.
- Post-rollback: provide rollback verification report and optional opt-in replay to compare outputs.

SLA & credits note:
- We consider SLA credit on a case-by-case basis. If you believe the incident materially impacted your service-level expectations, please open a ticket mentioning JIRA-CS-7218 and your tenant IDs; our CS billing team will coordinate.

Next steps and timelines (for CS to present to customers):
- 48–72 hours: finish internal postmortem and produce canonical replay consent form.
- 72 hours: deliver first tranche of evidence to any customers who signed consent.
- 1 week: stabilization summary and permanent fix rollout plan.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary CS lead: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai).
- Engineering incident lead: Evan Liu (evan@redwood.ai).
- If urgent, open JIRA-CS-7218 and mention tenant IDs; use #customer-ops in Slack for synchronous coordination.

Appendix — quick operator commands and artifact IDs (internal lab shorthand):
- Evidence run IDs: run-20260524-34a, run-20260524-34b (used to reproduce ordering).
- Reproduction note: run harness with --short-seq-mode and the small-batch concurrency profile.
- Sanity checks: token-order-diff.py --input evidence.json --output diff.txt

Notes to self / open questions (for internal review):
- Do we need a streamlined legal-approved consent text for EU customers? (Mariana to coordinate with Legal.)
- Should we offer a canned customer email template for each choice lane? CS to draft and attach.

End of draft.

Delivery checklist for CS before publishing to status page:
- [ ] Legal review of consent wording for EU/UK.
- [ ] Security scan of evidence bundle process.
- [ ] Internal postmortem link inserted.
- [ ] Customer-facing one-paragraph TL;DR finalized.
